AGRI.G6.CONSER.CONTROLLING_SOIL_EROSION..mastery: The child names splash erosion (raindrops knock soil loose), sheet erosion (a thin layer is washed away evenly), rill erosion (small channels cut in the soil) and gully erosion (deep channels), and names causes (heavy rain, bare ground, cutting trees, overgrazing, ploughing up and down a slope). The child does not say a gully is a thin layer. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the control for a site
say why a control works

find the false step in a learner's plan
AGRI.G6.CONSER.CONTROLLING_SOIL_EROSION..mastery: The child names ways to control erosion (terraces and contour ploughing across the slope, planting trees, grass or cover crops, mulching, grass strips, closing a gully with stones and planting it), says each works by slowing the water or holding the soil, and does not plough up and down a slope or leave it bare. This is the knowledge half of outcome b; doing it is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

AGRI.G6.CONSER.CONSERVING_WATER.SEEDBEDS.mastery: The child says a sunken bed (a bed dug below the ground level) holds water and suits a dry place, that a raised bed drains fast and suits a very wet place, that a flat bed lies between the two, and that mulch (dry grass or leaves on the bed) keeps the soil moist. Preparing a seedbed is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

AGRI.G6.CONSER.CONSERVING_WILD_ANIMALS.D.mastery: The child picks a deterrent that keeps the animal away without killing it (a scarecrow or shiny strips for birds, a beehive fence, a chilli fence or a trench for elephants, a thorn or live fence, noise from a tin or a guard dog), says wild animals must be kept away and not killed, and does not pick poison or a snare. Setting a deterrent up is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

AGRI.G6.FOOD_P.REARING_SMALL_DOMESTIC_A..mastery: The child says daily jobs are feeding on proper feed, giving clean water, and checking each animal, that the house is cleaned and kept dry, that animals are vaccinated and dewormed as advised, that a sick animal is separated and the adult or animal health worker is told, and that records are kept. The child does not say any scraps will do or that water is optional. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

AGRI.G6.PRODUC.CONSTRUCTING_MOIST_BED_G..mastery: The child says a moist bed garden is a sunken bed with layers of dry plant matter and manure under the topsoil and mulch on top, which holds water so that vegetables such as kale and spinach grow in dry times, puts the steps in order (choose a site near water, dig, add layers, add topsoil, plant, mulch, water), and does not say it is a raised bed. Building it is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
